Botulinum toxin type A, injections play a key role in managing focal spasticity in children with cerebral palsy (CP) by temporarily weakening overactive muscles.
By relaxing spastic muscles, they improve range of motion, enhance gait, reduce pain, and facilitate functional motor skills when combined with physiotherapy. 
Key Aspects of Botulinum toxin type A in Cerebral Palsy:
•	Targeted Relief: Injections directly target specific muscles causing stiffness (spasticity) in lower or upper limbs, allowing antagonist muscles to strengthen.
•	Multidisciplinary Approach: It is most effective when paired with other treatments like casting, orthotics (AFO/KAFO), and physical therapy.
•	Benefits: Key improvements include better joint alignment, reduced pain, improved gait patterns, and potentially delaying the need for surgical muscle-tendon lengthening.
•	Reversible Effect: The effects are not permanent, usually lasting a few months, and require regular, carefully planned, and timed sessions.
•	Risks: While generally safe, potential side effects include temporary weakness, muscle atrophy (which may not be fully reversible), pain at the injection site, or rarely, spread of the toxin.

Paediatric bone remodelling is the highly active, age-dependent process where immature bone reshapes itself after injury or during growth, often correcting significant angulation and malalignment. Driven by osteoblasts and osteoclasts in response to stress, it is most efficient in younger children, close to the growth plates (physes), and within the plane of joint motion. 
Key Aspects of Paediatric Bone Remodelling
Rapid Healing: Children's bones heal faster and remodel better than adults, with younger age directly correlating to higher, more complete remodelling potential.
Role of Growth Plates (Physes): Remodelling is most pronounced at the growing ends of bones. If a fracture is near the physis, the body can often correct significant angulation.
Mechanism of Correction: Remodelling occurs via asymmetric growth of the epiphysis and appositional remodeling, where new bone forms on the concave side of an angle while it is removed from the convex side.
Limits of Remodelling:
Angulation: High potential for correction, particularly in the plane of joint motion.
Translation (Side-by-side): Good potential for correction in younger children.
Rotation: Minimal potential to remodel; rotational deformities usually do not correct on their own.
Shortening: Can be corrected, often through overgrowth of the bone, particularly in the femur. 
Factors Affecting Remodelling
Age: Younger children have superior remodelling, while the capacity decreases as the child approaches skeletal maturity

featured_reviews.name: Akshay Jain
featured_reviews.review_text:
I underwent right ankle surgery under Dr. Ajay Shenvi. My family and friends have also consulted him in the past. I have absolutely no complaints about the doctor—he is excellent at his work and highly skilled.

However, I would advise patients and families to be cautious when dealing with the hospital staff. If you are making any payment, ensure that you receive an invoice for the exact amount paid. I understand that patients and their families are already under stress during such times, but unfortunately, some staff members seem to take advantage of this situation.

I paid approximately INR 1,80,000 for my surgery, but the invoice provided was for around INR 1,79,000. Initially, I discussed this with my family and decided to let it go. During my follow-up appointment after 15 days, I raised this issue with the reception. She initially asked me to prove the INR 1,000 difference, and once I showed the details, she suddenly acknowledged the discrepancy and redirected me to the ward nurse.

The ward nurse also appeared aware that an extra INR 1,000 had been collected and gave several unnecessary explanations. Although I considered discussing this with the doctor, I chose not to involve him. Eventually, I received a refund after my follow-up visit. The staff claimed they had noted it in their diary but forgot to inform me for 15 days, which is difficult to believe. They both were giving me unnecessary excuses and was making me feel that I am wrong because I raised after 15 days and in their view it is too late. They forgot that I underwent surgery and need some time for recovery. Really disappointed with the both staff and their behaviour for INR 1000.

The takeaway is simple: always verify your invoices and payment receipts. Do not assume everything is accurate—double-check the amounts you pay to them.

featured_reviews.name: Riddhi Sonigra
featured_reviews.review_text: This is regarding a spinal surgery done on my family member who was operated by Dr Welling. Surgery done was unsuccessful and had to be recorrected at Hinduja hospital. The diagnosis part was correct but the execution was extremely incorrect. The surgical procedure explained before surgery didn’t mention anything about the implant that was going to be placed but an implant was placed. A very small heavy stainless steel metal implant was placed on the spine which couldn’t support the spine for even 30 days. All orthopaedic surgeries are advised physiotherapy next day onwards but patient was advised complete bed rest for 2 months post surgery and was restricted to few movements only. Doctor started medicines which were to be started slowly to see if there was any reaction to it and then modified accordingly. But all the drugs were started together which deteriorated patients health. Patient was vomiting 15-20 times a day which caused severe electrolyte imbalance, dehydration and severe weakness. Doctor was unavailable at the time when the patient developed same issue for which she was operated and came in after a day. The patient had to go through severe trauma of going through two spinal surgeries within a span of 30 days along with mental and physical stress and an exhaustive process of treatment.
